files.purpose: This AppModel extension is the Hydra auto-merge coordinator: when "Merge when the team is done" (settings.hydraAutoMerge) is on, it lands a finished lead's job and its heads' files as a commit built from a scratch-index snapshot, on a stable per-chat hydra/<slug>-<6 chars of the lead id> branch (or on the checkout's current non-default branch), pushes it (force-pushed when it is the chat's own branch), opens a merge request through glab/gh/tea and merges it, then brings the checkout up to date without ever changing branch. It also decides which files are the job's (turn touched paths, head landings and head/lead tool edits, plus a checkout sweep since the first turn's checkpoint, minus other chats' reserved or blocking claims unless this job edited the file itself), splits the job per sidebar project, serialises merges app-wide (a job that finishes while another merges now waits in a 400 ms poll instead of being skipped), retries self-clearing failures quietly a minute later, and reports outcomes as HydraMergeRecord entries plus Hydra notes in the lead's timeline. At B3 the whole 'held' mechanism (a job waiting on another chat's files) is gone.

A blocking sibling claim now only removes that file from this merge, and only when this job's own tools or heads did not write it (ownEdits, 646-654). Every unmerged turn and every counted head of the job is settled by a completed run (667-669). Timeline.swift:271-272 confirms .held is no longer written and stays only so older records decode; the '.held' test at 157 now fires only for such legacy records.

QUEUEING: autoMergeHydraWork first checks setting, thread, Hydra on, runtime present, not merging, not already queued, ready (80-82). If any merge is running it sets isHydraMergeQueued, polls isAnyHydraMergeRunning every 400 ms (returning on cancellation), clears the flag in a defer, then re-reads every guard (98-100). B2 returned immediately and relied on the next resume sweep.

After a run whose outcomes contain neither .failed nor .deferred, a Task schedules resumeHydraMerges() (172-174); AppModel is @MainActor, so it runs only after this function has marked the work and cleared its flags.

NEW OUTCOME .deferred (25-27): a checkout mid-rebase/merge now schedules a quiet retry and returns .deferred with no record and no note (244-249; B2 recorded and posted 'a rebase or merge is underway'); losing readiness after the capture returns .deferred (304; B2 returned .failed). The caller returns before marking on .deferred just as on .failed (171).

fail() helper (226-237): detail = title(headline) + ": " + body for every project-pass failure; retryable failures schedule a 60 s retry (scheduleHydraMergeRetry, 411-423, one pending per chat via hasHydraMergeRetryPending); a failure whose detail equals the last record's (outcome .failed) returns .failed with no new record and no note; a retryable failure posts its note only when the two records before it are both retryable failures (suffix(2) checked before recording), so a first or second quiet failure is recorded without a note, and because identical details are de-duplicated before recording, a retryable failure that repeats the same text is never announced. Records carry retryable: true for retryable failures and nil otherwise.

PREPARE LOOP (271-331): up to three tries. On the chat's own branch it fetches origin and, when origin/<target> moved past HEAD, builds the tree on the remote with captureTree(paths:onto:from:); nil (overlapping changes) fails non-retryably with 'Hydra did not merge: `<target>` changed the same lines.'; the rebased tree's three-way results (merged) are later written into the checkout by syncDefaultBranch. alreadyOnMain now compares with the parent's tree (remote or HEAD). The diff and commit parent are the parent, the commit message is reused when the patch is unchanged, and a HEAD that moved after commitWork restarts the loop instead of failing; after three tries 'Hydra did not merge: the checkout kept moving.' (retryable).

Own branch: hydraBranchName's suffix is now the first six characters of lead.id.uuidString lowercased (880), so every try reuses one branch per chat; the ref is moved with the two-argument updateRef (unconditional, 339) and pushed with pushBranch(branch, force: true) (348), so a retry updates the open request. Non-own branch keeps updateRef(expecting: head) + resetIndex (342-345) and a non-forced push.

Merge request failures: HydraMergeRequestError.gitLabAuth -> non-retryable, body = its localizedDescription only (356-358); any other creation error -> retryable with the new 'next try opens the request' body (359-362); a nil URL or unparseable link -> retryable with 'The forge did not say where the request is. The next try opens it again.' (363-366); a failed merge -> retryable with 'The next try brings the request up to date with `<target>` and merges it.' (368-372). The generic catch now goes through fail(), so its record detail is project-prefixed and ends with the retry sentence (406-407), resolving the B2 record/note prefix asymmetry.

hydraCreateMergeRequest: after the first failed glab mr create, Git.existingRequestURL(in:web:) returns the already-open request for the branch (the text must contain 'already exist'; an https URL or a GitLab !<n> reference) before the auth and --recover handling (460-462).

hydraWork gains an 'edited' list (536-539) fed by head landing files (575), head timeline tool edits (590) and the lead's own tool edits (600-611, refactored with no change to 'reported'); ownEdits are these made relative to the checkout (653).
